### Observed differences

- In the later window, activity A04 appears in about 32% of traces instead of 14%, and its mean position shifts from about halfway through the trace to about 83% of the way through, i.e. it now occurs later. [OCC001, POS001]
- A04 now usually occurs after A25, A26, A27, A28 and A40: the share of traces where one of those activities precedes A04 rises from about 6% to about 28–29%, while the share where A04 precedes them drops to near zero. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]
- A19 and A20 now occur earlier (mean position from about 0.52 to about 0.37) and now precede A25 in about half of the traces, whereas before they followed A25 in about 40–56% of traces. [POS002, POS003, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013]
- Successor distributions change sharply: A19 and A20 now go to A25 in about 96% of their outgoing transitions (previously they went to A27/A28); A26 now goes to A27 in about 98% (previously about 54%); A27 now goes to A28 in about 98% (previously about 46%); A40 now goes to A19 or A20 in about 97% of transitions, instead of to A25 in about 94%. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR008]
- A43 now sometimes goes to A04 (about 33% of its transitions) instead of almost always to A44. [DIR009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reordering of a segment of the process: a path that previously ran from A40 through A25 and then to A19/A20 and A27/A28 now appears to run from A40 to A19/A20, then to A25, then to A26, A27 and A28, with A04 executed later and more often. This is supported directly by successor changes (DIR), relational order changes (REL), and position shifts (POS) that are consistent across multiple activities. A competing explanation—that the differences reflect sampling variation in variant frequencies—is unlikely given the number of distinct, mutually consistent indicators, although the evidence cannot rule out that some rare variants contributed to the observed shifts.
